1000501.etyen:
Borrowed from English Mars (“Mars, the company and chocolate-bar brand”), from the surname Mars of the founding family. The family business was established by Frank C. Mars and later developed into Mars, Incorporated. His son Forrest Mars Sr. moved to Britain in 1932 and created the Mars chocolate bar that year.
The company sense is a clipping of the full company name Mars Incorporated. The chocolate-bar sense uses the same family and company name. The deeper origin of the founding family's surname has not been securely established here.

en.g: a river in Nord-Odal municipality, Innlandet, Norway, flowing south into Storsjøen near Austvatn

1004597.etyen:
Ultimately unknown. Peter Andreas Munch connected the name group with a reconstructed verb *svirka, corresponding to Proto-Germanic *swerkaną (“to become dark”), reflected in Old English sweorcan (“to become dark, be obscured”). If this explanation is correct, the river name would have meant approximately “the dark one”. It has alternatively been compared with the sound-symbolic verb surkle (“to gurgle, burble; make a sloshing sound”).
Compare the Norwegian river names Sorka, Svarka, Sverka and Svorka.

1004853.etyen:
From Kongeriket (“the kingdom”) and Nederlandene (“the Low Countries”), translating Dutch Koninkrijk der Nederlanden (“Kingdom of the Netherlands”).
Parallel formations include Norwegian Nynorsk Kongeriket Nederlanda, Danish Kongeriget Nederlandene, German Königreich der Niederlande and English Kingdom of the Netherlands.
